speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your son's condition, could you describe his stool pattern, specifically noting the frequency, consistency, and color of his bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the baby is fussy, has decreased feeding, and has a distended, tender abdomen. Has he passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and if so, what did it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas since birth, and if so, when was his first meconium passed? I need to determine if there is a functional obstruction like Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to rule out a mechanical obstruction or severe motility issue. Has the baby passed any gas or stool in the last 24 hours, and when was his first meconium passed after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops with an empty rectum are classic for Hirschsprung disease, especially given the history of feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. Since the biopsy is unavailable, I will rely on the strong radiological evidence and clinical presentation to make my diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
